title: A fluorescence microscopy-based protocol for volumetric measurement of lysolecithin lesion-associated de- and re-myelination in mouse brain
protocol: Thaw one 20 μL aliquot of lysolecithin 1% and warm to 37°C.
Sonicate the thawed lysolecithin for 15 min if precipitates are formed.
Add 0.2 μL of Monastral blue solution to 20 μL of lysolecithin.
Keep the lysolecithin – Monastral blue solution at 37°C.
Weigh the mouse and inject the corresponding amount of MMF anesthesia intraperitoneally (0.5 mg/kg BW Medetomidine, 5 mg/kg BW Midazolam, 0.05 mg/kg BW Fentanyl).
Keep mice in a dark, warm space to ensure correct full anesthesia.
Prepare the Nanoliter injector.
Loosen the collet covering the gasket and plunger and the O-rings.
Clean and dry the O-rings thoroughly.
Break approximately 1.5 mm off the tip of a glass capillary using fine forceps.
Pass the capillary through the collet with the conical part facing the tip of the capillary.
Slide the capillary through the red O-ring from its blunt end so that the conical part points towards the collet and the tip of the capillary.
Fill the glass capillary with mineral oil from the non-pulled end.
Fill a 1 mL syringe with mineral oil.
Attach a MicroFil needle to the syringe and ensure that oil is being ejected through the needle.
Insert the MicroFil needle into the glass capillary from the blunt end, pushing it near the pulled end of the capillary.
Eject liquid into the glass capillary while slowly withdrawing the MicroFil needle until the capillary is completely full with oil.
Install a black O-ring onto the collet with the larger hole facing towards the injector.
Slide in a white spacer so that its flat side faces the injector and its recessed part receives the capillary.
Slide the filled glass capillary onto the plunger until it contacts the recessed part of the white spacer, causing some oil to leak out.
Clean away any leaked oil with a cotton swab.
Press the glass capillary towards the injector to avoid bubble formation within the oil.
Push the collet towards the aluminum barrel and screw it until it is finger tight.
Fill the glass capillary with lysolecithin – Monastral blue solution.
Set and run the Micro4Pump to inject 4000 nL at a rate of 2000 nL/min to push mineral oil out of the glass capillary.
Clean excessive oil from the tip of the glass capillary.
Run the Micro4Pump to withdraw 400 nL at a rate of 2000 nL/min to create a 1 mm-thick air bubble within the glass capillary.
Immerse the glass capillary into the lysolecithin – Monastral blue solution and withdraw 3600 nL of the solution at a rate of 1000 nL/min into the glass capillary.
Use a cotton swab wet with saline solution to stroke the tip of the glass capillary slightly.
Repeat stroking the tip every 5–10 min to prevent drying and clotting of the lysolecithin within the glass capillary.
Transfer the mouse from the dark, warm cage onto a heating pad.
Check for full anesthesia by testing the interdigital reflex on the paw.
Cover the eyes with a small drop of Bepanthen eye cream to protect them from drying out.
Cut hair from the head using scissors or alternatively, using a trimmer.
Using fine scissors or a thin scalpel, cut a 1 to 1.5 cm-long incision on the head skin to expose the mouse skull above the cortical hemispheres.
Visualize both the Bregma and Lambda intersections.
Place the mouse in the stereotaxic apparatus.
Fix the left ear bar to a predefined scale (e.g., 4 mm).
Fit the left ear canal of the mouse onto the left ear bar to expose the skull.
Hold the mouse head firmly while sliding the right ear bar into the right ear canal to expose the skull.
Fix the right ear bar to the same scale as the left ear bar.
Insert the incisor adapter into the mouse’s mouth until its incisors fit into the small opening in the adapter.
Gently pull out the tongue of the mouse slightly to allow for correct breathing.
Slightly pull back the incisor adapter to check for its correct position on the incisors.
Fix the incisor adapter securely.
Place the snout clamp just below the eyes using low pressure.
Ensure that no movement is possible when the mouse’s head is completely fixed in the stereotaxic apparatus.
Identify Bregma and Lambda on the animal's skull.
Move the capillary to Bregma so that the tip lightly touches it.
Reset all coordinates after touching Bregma.
Move the capillary to Lambda without changing the X coordinate, adjust Y and Z for light touch.
Check the Z coordinate at Lambda.
Adjust head position with the screw at the incisor adapter if the Z coordinate changes by more than +/- 50 μm between Bregma and Lambda.
Reset all coordinates at Bregma using the stereotaxic apparatus.
Move the glass capillary to X: −1 mm and Y: −0.1 mm relative to Bregma.
Lower the glass capillary carefully and mark the resulting position on the skull with a marker.
Raise the glass capillary to its highest position for protection.
Attach a 0.5 mm drill-bit to the Micro Drill and set the speed to 20,000 rpm.
Apply gentle pressure while holding the Micro Drill steady to make a single burr-hole at the marked site on the skull.
Stop drilling immediately upon noticing a sudden drop in hand holding the Micro Drill.
Remove any small pieces of remaining skull with a sharp object like forceps or blade to expose the brain.
Apply saline solution to the hole to keep the brain moist.
Lower the glass capillary again just to the brain surface to confirm correct positioning.
Inject a small volume of fluid while visually controlling the tip of the glass capillary to ensure it is not clogged.
Lower the glass capillary into the brain parenchyma until the Z coordinate is −1.45 mm.
Raise the glass capillary to the Z coordinate −1.4 mm.
Set the Micro4Pump settings to inject 1000 nL at a speed of 100 nL/min.
Inject lysolecithin into the brain parenchyma by running the program set in the Micro4Pump.
Wait for 2 more minutes after completing the program.
Slowly raise the glass capillary until it is out of the brain.
Remove the mouse from the stereotaxic device by releasing the incisor and ear adapters.
Transfer the mouse to a warm pad.
Inject 0.05 mg/kg BW of buprenorphine subcutaneously.
Apply saline solution onto the skull to ensure brain and skull moisture.
Pull the skin edges of the incision together.
Stitch using braided absorbable suture (suture 4/0 or 5/0 works).
Inject 2.5 mg/kg BW of Atipamezole, 0.5 mg/kg BW Flumazenil, and 1.2 mg/kg BW Naloxon subcutaneously to terminate the anesthesia.
Clean away the Bepanthene from the eyes.
Keep the mouse in a warm, preferably dark space until full recovery from the anesthesia.
Monitor the mouse 24 hours after injection by checking its weight.
Inject 0.05 mg/kg of Buprenorphin subcutaneously 24 hours after the injection as analgesia.
Monitor the mouse 48 hours after injection by checking its weight.
Inject 0.05 mg/kg of Buprenorphin subcutaneously 48 hours after the injection as analgesia.
Monitor the mouse 72 hours after injection by checking its weight.
Prepare 4% paraformaldehyde solution and 1× PBS.
Anesthetize the mouse by injecting 150 μL of 10% ketamine and 2% xylazine intraperitoneally.
Expose the heart, insert a venofix needle into the left ventricle and open the right atrium.
Perfuse using a peristaltic pump with 5 mL of 1× PBS followed by 30 mL of 4% PFA at a rate of 2 mL/min.
Remove the brain and keep overnight in 4% PFA at 4°C for 24 hours.
Wash the brain three times in 1× PBS.
Transfer the brain to cryoprotecting sucrose solution for 2 days or until the brain sinks to the bottom of the tube.
Place a wet paper on top of a metallic blade on dry ice.
Apply a drop of Tissue Tek O.C.T. on the blade.
Position the brain with its caudal end on the paper covered in O.C.T.
Section the brain coronally starting from the most dorsal part towards the ventral part to avoid tissue destruction at the lesion site.
Cryosection the demyelinated lesion ensuring serial sectioning.
Cool down an aluminum surface on dry ice (e.g., a blade).
Dry excess sucrose around the brain and cut the cerebellum off (to provide a flat surface).
Dip a 1 cm x 1 cm square of paper in water, then place it on top of the cooled aluminum surface, on top of dry ice.
Add a small drop of Tissue-Tek O.C.T onto the paper.
Place the brain on top of the paper with the flat surface on top.
Cover the sample in pre-cooled aluminum foil.
Keep the sample at −80°C.
Cut serial 15-μm-thick coronal sections of the lesion using a cryostat.
Directly mount the sections on Superfrost glass slides.
Collect additional sections before and after the lesion to ensure full coverage.
Section from the dorsal side through to the ventral side of the brain.
Collect several sections before and after the lesion to ensure acquisition of the entire lesion.
Air-dry the sections for 16–20 hours (overnight) at room temperature.
Transfer and keep the sections at -20°C.
Transfer the glass slides to be stained to a 37°C environment for 30 minutes.
Rinse the slides with 1× PBS, three times for 5 minutes each.
Permeabilize the tissue using 1× PBS containing 0.3% Triton X for 10 minutes.
Incubate the sections with a blocking solution for 1 hour.
Encircle the sections with a hydrophobic PAP Pen to ensure liquid stays on top of the sections.
Dilute IBA1 antibodies at a concentration of 1:2000 in staining solution.
Incubate the sections with primary antibodies for 16 hours at 4°C.
Continue incubation with the same solution for an additional hour at room temperature.
Wash the sections with 1× PBS, three times for 5 minutes each.
Dilute the anti-rabbit Alexa 555 secondary antibody at a concentration of 1:1000 in staining solution.
Incubate the sections with secondary antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash the sections with 1× PBS, three times for 5 minutes each.
Dilute Fluoromyelin (1:400) and DAPI (1:1000) in 1× PBS.
Incubate sections with Fluoromyelin and DAPI for 15 minutes.
Wash the sections with 1× PBS for 3× 10 minutes.
Dip slides in ddH2O.
Remove excess water using a tissue and protect slides from light until all water evaporates (approximately 10 minutes).
Cover sections using a glass coverslip (#1.5 thickness) with Mowiol as the mounting medium.
Dry the covered sections overnight at room temperature for 16–20 hours.
Store the slides at 4°C until imaging.
Acquire fluorescence images of the stained sections for three channels (DAPI, Fluoromyelin, AF555).
Use standard settings for multi-channel acquisition with either an epifluorescence microscope or a laser-scanning confocal microscope.
Select an objective with a field of view large enough to fit the lesion region (e.g., 10×).
Acquire and merge tile-scan images if the field of view is smaller than the whole lesion.
Set the excitation intensity and detection gain for each channel so that fluorophores are properly excited but not saturated.
Use the same pixel size for all acquisitions.
Use the same excitation and detection settings for all acquisitions.
Identify demyelinated lesions as areas of corpus callosum with FluoroMyelin-negative signal and prominent IBA1+ cell accumulation.
Image all demyelinated areas in a specific order to track lesion sequence.
Save images consecutively numbered as individual gray-scale .tiff files or inside an image container file.
Quantify the demyelinated area using ImageJ/FIJI macro "Macro_Analyse_Lesion_Area.ijm".
Open the macro in FIJI by dragging and dropping the .ijm file into ImageJ/FIJI or through File→Open… menu.
Run the macro to analyze areas of clustered IBA1+ cells and compute lesion volume using an iPython script.
Select the option "Analyse single image container file".
Check the option “Save ROI Selections” if you wish to save the area selections.
Give the basic name of the output folder where result text files and ROIs will be saved.
The output folder name will include the date and time when the macro runs.
Press OK to proceed.
Select the folder containing the image files or the image container file for analysis.
Open each selected image along with a pop-up message asking to select the region of interest.
Delineate the area of Fluoromyelin negative staining or IBA1+ clustered cells as required.
Click OK after selecting the region of interest.
Repeat steps until all images are processed.
Copy the area measurements for each section in an excel file.
List animal names corresponding to each section in the first column of the excel file.
Calculate and specify the radii r of the corresponding sections using the formula \(r = \sqrt{\frac{A}{\pi}}\) in the third column.
Run iPython 2.7.
Input the prepared excel file into the script.
Input the known distance between consecutive sections in μm.
Calculate the volume between sections using the truncated cone volume formula.
Sum up single volumes between all sections per animal.
Output a file containing animal names and their corresponding lesion volume.
